doc.title: Arthur Baron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Getting gig unemployment through a state senator's office
summary: After failing online, Baron got help from a senator's office to apply and receive Pandemic Unemployment, and urges others to do the same.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: I didn’t either. That was the ownership by the musicians. No there were several other kinds of freelance work that was called the “gig employment.” And so musicians held onto that idea, as far as I can see, the way they talk about it. Well here’s what happened: a friend of mine who is politically active, and I know this is not about music but this could help musicians. Because it was impossible. I could not make the website work. And then when I was getting close I got locked out of it. A friend of mine is very politically active, who I am often signing petitions for. I just on a lark I called her. And she found my state senator’s office in Albany, and she got a local person there to contact me, you know, someone who works, you know a helper with the senator. And she connected me with unemployment people who called me. And here I mean it is a really detailed thing. You have to apply for the regular, the not gig unemployment, the regular like if you had say a nine to five, five days a week kind of job. You have to apply for that and obviously you will get denied. Then you have to apply for the gig unemployment, or what they call the pandemic — PAU or something, Pandemic something Unemployment. And unemployment called me on the phone, spent about 45 minutes with me. They were actually filling it out. I wasn’t online, I was just on the phone. So this is really important. I hope your listeners hear this, find your local senator’s office, state senator, and call them. And so if you get people as nice as I got they not only filled it all out online but they walked me through everything, got me denied on the same call, and then applied for the Pandemic Unemployment. And I got it, like a week later or something, it kicked in. I mean so I hope, it’s not a musical idea but — well it is musical in that a lot of musicians are in this situation.
That’s really good information, I had no idea.
Yeah. You know and I’ve told people that, because the person that helped me can’t help you like if you wanted to do it because you’re upstate New York, you have a different senator I would think.
